texts.preamble: M/S Tommy Hilfiger Europe B.V vs Amarjeet Singh on 23 May, 2023 In The Court Of Mr. Satyabrata Panda, Adj-04, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cs (Comm) No.382 Of 2019 Date of institution:19.12.20
texts.facts: The plaintiff has filed the present suit against the defendants for permanent injunction and other reliefs in respect of infringement of the plaintiff's trademark. It is stated in the plaint that the plaintiff is a company organized and existing under the laws of the Netherlands. It is stated that the plaintiff was established in the year 1977. The plaintiff is engaged in the business of manufacture, distribution and sale of a wide range of apparels, fragrances, footwear, watches, wallets, shoes, belts, home furnishings and other accessories and other allied/related products (hereinafter referred to as "the said goods" and "the said business"). It is stated that the plaintiff was founded by Mr. Thomas Jacob Hilfiger. Ever since its establishment, the plaintiff has been using the M/S Tommy Hilfiger Europe B.V vs Amarjeet Singh on 23 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57536030/ 2 word/mark TOMMY HILFIGER, TOMMY, TOMMY GIRL logo/label and the FLAG Logo as a trademark and TOMMY HILFIGER as an essential part of its trade name in relation to its said goods and business. The plaintiff over a period of time has been using its said trade mark in various stylized/artistic formats/labels and which have been created and are being created over a period of time viz. (FLAG logo), (TOMMY HILFIGER label), TOMMY HILFIGER (which are hereinafter collectively referred to as "The said trademark"). It is stated that the colour combination of blue, red and white and their arrangement is the key and essential feature of the overall get up of TOMMY HILFIGER logo, FLAG logo and TOMMY HILFIGER label, and the same are liable to be protected against misappropriation, imitation and misuse being valuable intellectual property rights of the plaintiff. The plaintiff has filed CS (COMM) NO.382 OF 2019 M/s Tommy Hilfiger Europe B.V VS Amarjeet Singh & ors. page no.3 copy of its trademark along with the plaint. It is further stated that apart from the aforesaid registrations plaintiff's various others applications for registration of said trade mark are pending in India. It is stated that the plaintiff's all registrations are valid and subsisting till date. It is stated that the plaintiff's pending applications are likely to be allowed in due course after completion of all formalities. 31. It is stated that the plaintiff learnt about the defendant's impugned trade mark in the Last week of October, 2013 when the plaintiff came across the impugned goods of the defendants in New Delhi market. Being aggrieved thereby, the plaintiff caused an inquiry in the market, which revealed that the defendants had just about in the month of September, 2013, adopted and starting using the impugned trade mark/label in relation to their impugned goods. Vide order dated 19/12/2013, summons were issued in the suit and interim injunction was passed under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 CPC and local commissioners were appointed to seize the infringing goods. 34. The defendants were served with the summons in the suit. All the defendants, except the defendant no.10 filed the written statements in which they denied liability. Subsequently, the other defendants also stopped appearing in the suit and all the defendants were proceeded ex parte.
texts.arguments: TOMMY, TOMMY HILFIGER, TOMMY GIRL and GLAG Logo (including logos) have come to be inextricably associated with the plaintiff and connote and denote the goods and business originating from the plaintiff and none else. 12. It is stated that on account of extensive media coverage through newspaper advertisements, articles, television programmes, fashion events and their telecast which have circulation in India or footfalls in India as well as on account of millions of Indians traveling abroad and, getting exposure of "Tommy Hilfiger" branded products in markets and advertisements in magazines and hoardings as well as through members of fashion industry, the trade mark(s) of the plaintiffs enjoyed spillover and trans-border reputation in India prior to 2004. The goods of plaintiffs are now available for sale in open commercial market through its Indian franchisee, namely GVM International which is "Murjani Group" in India since 2004. The overall sale of accessory products including perfumes/fragrances under the house mark TOMMY HILFIGER in India for the financial year 2006-07 has been over Rs. 100 Crores. 13. It is stated that the plaintiff has regularly and continuously been promoting its said distinctive trademark and the goods and business thereunder through extensive advertisements, publicities, promotions and marketing & marketing research and the plaintiff has been spending enormous amounts of moneys, efforts, skills and time thereon. The plaintiff has been doing so through various means and modes including through the visual, print and electronic media, in leading Newspapers, trade literature & magazines, word of mouth, over the internet etc and all CS (COMM) NO.382 OF 2019 M/s Tommy Hilfiger Europe B.V VS Amarjeet Singh & ors. page no.8 of which have tremendous reach, availability and circulation world over including in India. That several renowned actors and models are the brand ambassadors of the plaintiff. 14. It is stated that in view of the aforesaid including the plaintiff's priority in adoption and use thereof, the plaintiff's said trade mark has acquired enviable and enduring goodwill, reputation and users, and which the plaintiff owns, in the international markets including in India, wherein in addition to the aforesaid the plaintiff also enjoys trans-boarder reputation and users as extending into India. . It is stated that the plaintiff invests heavily in R & D and its products are known for their highest standards of quality, safety, innovation and reliability and there is an ever-increasing demand therefor. The members of the trade, industry, the consumers and CS (COMM) NO.382 OF 2019 M/s Tommy Hilfiger Europe B.V VS Amarjeet Singh & ors. page no.10 general public at large world over and in India are well aware of the plaintiff, the plaintiff's said trade mark and the plaintiff's said goods and business thereunder. It is stated that in view of the plaintiffs' proprietary rights both statutory and common law in its said trademark, its goodwill & reputation, and its copyrights, the plaintiff has the exclusive right to the use thereof and nobody can be permitted to use the same or any other deceptively similar trade mark/trade name/ copyrights thereto in any manner whatsoever in relation to any specification of goods without the leave and license of the plaintiff. 21. The plaintiff has along with the plaint filed specimens of defendants' impugned goods bearing the impugned trade mark. It is stated CS (COMM) NO.382 OF 2019 M/s Tommy Hilfiger Europe B.V VS Amarjeet Singh & ors. page no.11 that in fact the defendants are indulging in counterfeiting the tags, buttons, labels, packaging and other accessories to be used in the finished products in complete violation of plaintiff's statutory and common law right in the said trademark and copyright. 25. It is stated that the defendants by their impugned adoption and user of the impugned trade mark are violating the plaintiff's aforesaid trade mark and CS (COMM) NO.382 OF 2019 M/s Tommy Hilfiger Europe B.V VS Amarjeet Singh & ors. page no.12 thereby passing off and enabling others to pass off their goods and business as that of the plaintiff as well as diluting the plaintiff's proprietary rights therein. The defendants are further infringing the plaintiff's said trade mark, which is inter alia duly registered under different numbers. It is stated that the defendants are guilty of falsification, unfair and unethical trade practices. 28. It is stated that due to the defendants' impugned activities, the plaintiff is suffering huge losses both in business and in reputation and such losses are incapable of being assessed in monetary terms. The ld. counsel for the plaintiff has submitted that the plaintiff has proved its case on the basis of the ex parte evidence led. It is submitted that the evidence filed by the plaintiff was unrebutted and uncontroverted. It is submitted that as such the plaintiff would be entitled to decree in terms of the CS (COMM) NO.382 OF 2019 M/s Tommy Hilfiger Europe B.V VS Amarjeet Singh & ors. page no.19 prayer clauses of the plaint. It is further submitted that the defendants have deliberately avoided the proceedings and have also prevented the seizure of the goods by the local commissioners. It is submitted that the defendants are indulging in counterfeiting and unfair trade practices, and cannot be permitted to take advantage of their own wrong and that the case calls for punitive damages. In this manner, the defendants have prevented seizure of infringing goods while at CS (COMM) NO.382 OF 2019 M/s Tommy Hilfiger Europe B.V VS Amarjeet Singh & ors. page no.20 the same time conveniently avoiding the present proceedings. As held by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Microsoft Corporation Vs.Rajendra Pawar and Anr. reported as2008 (36) PTC 697 (Del.), awarding punitive damages prevents the erring party from taking advantage of its own wrong by escaping prosecution or detection. Reference in this regard is also made to LT Foods Ltd. v. Saraswati Trading Co. 2022/DHC/004806, Proctor & Gamble Company v. Joy Creators 2011 (450) PTC 541 Del, Louis Vuitton Malletier Vs. Iqbal Singh 2019 SCC online DEL 7879: (2019) 258 DLT 760, and Whatman International Ltd Vs. P. Mehta and Ors, 2019 SCC online Del 6856: (2019) 257 DLT 472.
